what_its_for: Sirolimus is used to prevent your body from rejecting a transplanted kidney. It works by suppressing your immune system so it does not attack the new organ. It may also be used for certain rare lung diseases and other conditions as directed by your doctor.
how_to_take: Take sirolimus by mouth once a day, at the same time every day. You can take it with or without food, but always take it the same way each time — either always with food or always without food. Swallow tablets whole; do not crush, chew, or split them. If you are taking the liquid form, use only the special syringe provided in the package to measure your dose. Mix the liquid with at least 2 ounces (60 mL) of water or orange juice — do not use grapefruit juice or any other liquid. Stir the mixture well and drink it right away. Then rinse the cup with more water or orange juice and drink that too, to make sure you get the full dose.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your body size, other medications, and blood test results. A common starting dose after a kidney transplant is 6 mg on the first day, then 2 mg once daily. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on regular blood level tests called 'trough levels.' Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store sirolimus tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep tablets in their original blister pack and protect them from light and moisture. For the liquid form, store the bottles in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Once you open a bottle of liquid, use it within 30 days. You may keep opened bottles at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for a short time if needed, but use within 15 days if stored at room temperature. Keep all forms away from children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice entirely — they can cause too much sirolimus to build up in your body and increase side effects. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds, as sirolimus increases your risk of skin cancer. Wear sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors. Avoid live vaccines (such as the live flu vaccine, MMR, or chickenpox vaccine) while on sirolimus without talking to your doctor first. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, especially those with infections, because this medicine lowers your immune system. Tell all of your doctors and pharmacists about every medication, supplement, and herbal product you take, especially St. John's Wort, antifungal drugs, and antibiotics, as many drugs interact with sirolimus.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: signs of infection such as fever, chills, sore throat, or unusual tiredness; signs of kidney problems like decreased urination or swelling in your legs or feet; shortness of breath, chest pain, or a new cough; unusual bleeding or bruising; severe stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhea; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (allergic reaction); changes in your skin such as new sores, bumps, or moles; or any signs of high cholesterol like yellow fatty deposits under the skin. Also contact your doctor if you feel your transplanted organ is being rejected, such as pain or tenderness at the transplant site.
when_it_works: Sirolimus starts working to protect your transplanted kidney right away, but you will not 'feel' it working directly. Your doctor will monitor your blood levels and kidney function through regular lab tests to confirm the medicine is working at the right level. It is very important to keep all of your lab appointments and doctor visits. Do not stop taking sirolimus without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): Use with caution. Your doctor may monitor you more closely for infections and other side effects. Children: Sirolimus is approved for children aged 13 years and older for kidney transplant rejection prevention. Pregnancy: Sirolimus can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for 12 weeks after stopping the medication. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking sirolimus, as it may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Liver disease: If you have liver problems, your doctor may need to lower your dose and will monitor you more carefully.
